events.title: The Great Dying
events.detail: About 252 million years ago the Siberian Traps erupt for hundreds of thousands of years, heating the planet and souring the seas. Some 90% of ocean species die out.

events.title: The first dinosaurs
events.detail: Small, two-legged dinosaurs such as Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus run through the river valleys of Ischigualasto, in what is now Argentina.

events.title: Lava splits Pangaea
events.detail: Floods of lava pour out along the rift between North America and Africa. The end-Triassic extinction follows, clearing the way for the dinosaurs.

events.title: The Atlantic opens
events.detail: North America pulls away from Africa and new sea floor starts to form between them: the central Atlantic, the first ocean to split Pangaea.

events.title: Dinosaurs rule; first birds
events.detail: Giant sauropods like Brachiosaurus roam the land, and Archaeopteryx, half dinosaur, half bird, glides over the lagoons of southern Germany.

events.title: First flowers
events.detail: Flowering plants appear. One of the oldest known, Montsechia, grew underwater in the lakes of Spain. Within 40 million years flowers cover most landscapes.

events.title: South America splits off
events.detail: Africa and South America unzip from south to north, and the South Atlantic floods in. Their coastlines still fit together like puzzle pieces.

events.title: India sets sail
events.detail: India breaks from Madagascar and races north at up to 15 cm a year, faster than any continent today, across the shrinking Tethys Ocean.

events.title: The asteroid strikes
events.detail: A 10 km asteroid hits Mexico's Yucatán. Wildfires and a long dark winter wipe out the dinosaurs, except birds, and three-quarters of all species.

events.title: Europe leaves Greenland
events.detail: The North Atlantic opens between Greenland and Norway, and huge lava flows build the Faroe Islands and the cliffs of Northern Ireland.

events.title: India hits Asia
events.detail: After 40 million years adrift, India crashes into Asia. The Tethys Ocean closes and the collision starts to push up Tibet.

events.title: Australia breaks free
events.detail: Australia speeds north away from Antarctica. A cold current now circles Antarctica, and by 34 million years ago its ice sheet has formed.

events.title: The Red Sea opens
events.detail: Arabia tears away from Africa. The rift floods to form the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, and Arabia swings north-east into Asia.

events.title: The Himalaya rise
events.detail: India keeps pushing into Asia, crumpling its edge into the world's highest mountains. Everest's summit is limestone formed on the floor of the Tethys.

events.title: Panama joins the Americas
events.detail: A land bridge rises between North and South America. Animals cross both ways, and ocean currents shift, helping to cool the planet.

events.title: The Ice Ages begin
events.detail: Ice sheets grow and melt again across North America and Europe dozens of times. The last one retreated about 11,700 years ago.

events.title: Homo sapiens appears
events.detail: Our species emerges in Africa about 300,000 years ago. The oldest known fossils come from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco.
